title: The Stone Milestone
story:
James left South Gate Avenue behind as the tall pine trees began to thin and the cobblestones gave way to packed mountain earth. He walked steadily, feeling the gentle weight of the brass pocket compass bumping against his ribs and the familiar leather strap bound with Mateo's colorful threads resting securely across his shoulder. Every step took him further from the comforting bustle of Oakhaven and closer to the wild, mist-softened embrace of the foothills.

Along the winding dirt track, he paused beside a weathered stone milestone half-swallowed by emerald moss and bright yellow mountain wildflowers. James pulled out his magnifying lens on its green ribbon to inspect the carved, faded numbers etched into the stone by human hands long ago. He traced the rough edges with a careful finger, wondering how many travelers had stopped right here to look up toward the towering heights of Cloudveil Ridge.

Following a sudden rustle in the roadside ferns, a bright blue mountain jay landed on a low branch, tilting its head to study James with intelligent, glossy eyes. James did not move a muscle, remembering his quiet forest home in the Great Canopy and the unspoken language shared with all creatures of the wild. After a long moment of shared silence, the bird darted upward into the damp canopy of leaves, leaving behind only the rustle of foliage and the fresh scent of pine resin.

With the sun beginning its slow descent behind the western ridges, casting long, golden shadows across the ascending trail, James whispered his habitual formal greeting to the wide-open horizon: 'Pleased to meet you, whatever comes next.' He adjusted his canvas-strapped treasures, stepped past the milestone, and continued his solitary climb into the foothills.
location: The Lower Foothills, ascending toward Cloudveil Ridge
